title: Change the building code only when the benefits clearly exceed the costs
action: Commission an independent review of building regulation at all levels of government, including the National Construction Code's objectives and governance, and adopt future code changes only where an impact analysis shows a net benefit and no cheaper alternative exists. Limit state and council additions to the code.
why: Several recent code changes were adopted although their own impact analysis showed a net cost, raising the cost of every new home. State and local variations also stop builders using the same designs nationally.

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: While a number of changes to the NCC have passed a regulatory impact assessment (RIA), frequently it has been the case that either the accompanying RIA does not recommend the change or the cost benefit analysis within the RIA shows a net cost to society.

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: Governments should undertake an independent review of building regulations at the federal, state and territory, and local government levels. This would include reviewing the aims and objectives of the NCC, its effectiveness, and its governance arrangements and membership.

progress.what: In August 2025 the Australian Government said it would work with the states to pause further residential changes to the code until mid-2029, excluding essential safety and quality changes.

tradeoffs: Energy efficiency and accessibility rules have benefits beyond productivity (lower bills, emissions, access for people with disability) that a cost-benefit test should count.
